sources.reviewed_note: Rebased our stack onto upstream tag v0.10.0 (2026-09-11, 'Initial build for Deep North'), which is the tip of master - there are no commits after the tag. Read the delta as a whole rather than commit by commit: 2774 upstream commits since our old base 50d333d. One of our seven was dropped by the rebase as already upstream ('Remove unused using that breaks builds outside Visual Studio'), and one new one was needed: v0.10.0 targets release-day 1.0.0 and references UpscaledFrameBuffer.UpdateCurrentRenderScale and m_targetResolutionVertical, neither of which exists in 1.0.12, so the frame-scaling patch was removed. Filed as vhp-8mo.
sources.local_changes: Branch neuralyze/v0.10.0: seven commits on upstream v0.10.0. Six carried over from neuralyze/local (non-VR HarmonyPrepare guards, csproj SkipReleasePackaging condition, the BodyPose workaround, startup-stage reporting, name-based tracker role resolution, and the Mono/Linux plus no-base-assetbundle build fixes) and one new: 'Drop the frame-scaling patch Valheim 1.0 removed the target of'. The old neuralyze/local branch is left where it was as a record of what shipped before. Built on this host with scripts/build-valheimvr.sh against build/latest-1.0.12, a publicized 1.0.12 reference set - see build/README-1.0.12-refs.md, because the build cannot be reproduced against build/latest, which is the pre-1.0 client.
sources.published_note: GPL-3.0 source offer. Branch neuralyze/local pushed to the fork 2026-08-25 at 23f0ce4526cd and publicly reachable; the portal links it from the world page and from the release pages of releases carrying a flat_companion or vr_runtime (PORTAL_VHVR_SOURCE_URL). Correspondence is anchored per binary, not per release version, because release versions are the portal's and mean nothing upstream: each published ValheimVRMod.dll gets a tag shipped/valheimvrmod-<first 12 hex of its sha256> on the commit it was built from. Pushed so far: shipped/valheimvrmod-f879224e030c -> 23f0ce4526cd, the DLL inside vr-runtime-2.2.5-nospawnprobe.zip served as hrafnheim-vr 2.5.111 and doggerland/storgard/vangard-vr 2.5.36. mcs is not reproducible - two compiles of one tree differ in ~77800 of 600064 bytes - so a build is matched by size plus source markers, not by hash.
sources.correspondence_gap: Audited 2026-08-26 by hashing ValheimVRMod.dll inside all 1793 published zips under the artifact root. Seven distinct binaries are published and exactly one carries a shipped/ tag, so the previous claim that every published build is tagged was wrong about six of them; the offer text on the pages has been corrected to say what is true per binary. Two of the seven can never be given a tag: 3fe2ce08 (the Flat companion, 147 releases) and c2519916 (an earlier Flat companion, 2 releases). Each holds part of commit 1d6ea02 without the rest of it - both carry the two "Non-VR companion mode" literals that enter the history only at 1d6ea02, 3fe2ce08 lacks the HarmonyPrepare typeref added by 5ea5183 (an ancestor of 1d6ea02) and c2519916 has it, but neither has 1d6ea02's own LogDiagnostic - and no commit can hold a descendant's strings without its ancestor's, nor half of a single commit. The cause is that the seven commits were authored on 2026-08-18 by grouping finished changes into themed commits rather than replaying how the tree evolved: the non-VR branch was written by 07-26 and HarmonyPrepare and LogDiagnostic by 07-28, but they were committed in the opposite order, so builds taken from the tree in between fall between the commits. Correcting an earlier note: the reflog does not start 2026-08-18, it starts 2026-07-26 04:15:44 with the clone of upstream at a10f24fc - 43 minutes before 3fe2ce08 was compiled - and it still does not help, because the intermediate tree was never committed. Searched and not found: no commit, no stash, no dangling object (the four dangling blobs are the vhvr-0.9.21*.zip archives), and no second copy of the source - a find for ValheimVRMod.cs across every mounted big drive returns exactly one checkout. Closing those two therefore needs a rebuild from a commit on the branch and a republish, which is a deliberate publish decision and not a repo change; until then the offer names both binaries and says we cannot name their revision, which is the honest state rather than a discharged-looking one.

sources.why: The container the world operation scripts drive. valheim_provision.py reads its default.env for the PGID a world's mounts are chowned to.
sources.reviewed_note: Read all 18 commits and the 14 files they touch. Material to us: Debian 12 then 13 base-image upgrades with 32-bit glibc restored, busybox cron replacing Debian vixie-cron, a UMASK calculation change that would land on the world directories provisioning chowns, and secrets support. The libdoorstop env-var rename (DOORSTOP_ENABLED/DOORSTOP_TARGET_ASSEMBLY) is already in our tree: our local commit 3ad0632 made the same fix independently, so upgrading converges and that part of our patch can be dropped. Upgrade deferred to a maintenance window because it replaces the base image under four live worlds; filed as a bead.
sources.local_changes: Four local commits, none of them upstream, published to https://github.com/neuralyze/valheim-server-docker branch neuralyze/local (we have no push access to community-valheim-tools, so that fork is the only off-host copy): 40252fce 'Update local Valheim server runtime', 3f736897 'Apply directory permissions to Valheim 1.0 world directories', 43844851 'Sync BepInEx patchers so preloader patches survive a rebuild', and f000f97f 'Never sync the download cache over the install when the update failed'. The last one is load-bearing: valheim-updater's download-failure branch logged "an existing version was found locally - using it" and then fell through to 'rsync -a --delete dl/ server/', which overwrote a correct 1.0.12 install with a stale 0.221.12 cache and reported it as "already the latest version". That silently downgraded three worlds on 2026-09-13 and emptied their saves - see bead vhp-oxn. Note also that docker-compose.yaml carries uncommitted operator changes (CONFIG_DIR/DATA_DIR made required rather than defaulting to a shared directory, WEBMAP_PORT dropped); those are deliberate and predate this session.
